title: Console walkthrough — Usage analytics & cost breakdown (Suncrest Retail)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Suncrest team through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and a model/route cost breakdown. Discussed token-level cost attribution, batching and KV caching impact on unit economics, and security requirements (KMS/SOC2/SSO). Agreed next steps to share pricing, security docs, and run a pilot with sample traffic.

next_steps: Jordan to send pricing + SOW template
Priya to upload benchmark spreadsheet and suggested config

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Start Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Mike Adler (Suncrest CTO), Lena Huang (Suncrest Head of ML), Sanjay Patel (Infra)

Summary (auto): short walkthrough of Console usage analytics, deep-dive into per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. Security questions on KMS and SOC 2. Agreed to pilot and share artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan, i'm the AE on this account. priya from our solutions eng team will do most of the console walk, i'll chime in for pricing and contract q's. mike, lena, sanjay — thanks for taking the time. can i get quick intros?
[00:15] Mike (Suncrest): yeah, mike here, cto. lena is head of ML, sanjay runs infra and networking. our use case is store-assistant and customer support routing, mostly inference for chat and classification, mixed seq lengths.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): awesome. i'll share my screen — starting with the usage analytics overview. this is the per-tenant view, you can change time windows, group by model or route. note: some fields in the export are auto-summarized, so if you want raw token logs we can export as csv or s3 link.
[00:48] Priya (Redwood): so here on the chart we show individual route qps, median latency, and token spend per route. you can toggle cost attribution to show per-token cost or per-request cost depending on how you bill internally.
[01:10] Lena (Suncrest): quick q — token spend per route, does that include batching and cache savings? like if we do prefix caching for repeated prompts will that reduce the token spend shown?
[01:22] Priya (Redwood): yes — the spend visualization accounts for KV caching and batching effects where we can attribute saved tokens. small caveat the exported line items will show the raw request length and the effective billed tokens after caching, but the UI attempts to estimate savings. sometimes the transcriber shows KV "cash" which is dumb, but it's cash, it's cache.
[01:40] Mike (Suncrest): heh, noted. how accurate is the per-route break down if we have shared models between routes?
[01:48] Priya (Redwood): we tag requests at the routing layer so even if the same model is used for multiple routes, the analytics can attribute by route, by customer route id. we also have model version tagging so you can split by model v1/v2 during rollouts.
[02:05] Jordan (Redwood): just to add — that tagging is part of the SDK and the request header. it's a small instrument change but it unlocks the per-route visibility which customers find super helpful for chargebacks.
[02:20] Sanjay (Suncrest): what about the token-level cost math? can you show the cost breakdown per model?
[02:28] Priya (Redwood): yep, moving to the cost breakdown panel. here we show cost per token bucketed by model type and hardware variant. you can filter on hosted vs dedicated. the UI also surfaces unit economics: tokens per dollar, and estimated monthly spend given your qps profile.
[02:50] Priya (Redwood): for example this route is using an open 7B model on shared hosted infra — you can see higher variance in latency but lower committed cost. if you pin it to dedicated capacity the cost per token improves for sustained traffic, but there's a monthly commit.
[03:10] Lena (Suncrest): so dedicated is only better if we have sustained throughput. we have spikes during promo windows, is there burst support?
[03:20] Priya (Redwood): yes, dedicated has configurable autoscale and burst to hosted capacity. the console shows projected overspill costs if you hit burst. that projection is what we use in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:34] Mike (Suncrest): can we run a simulation? like given our traffic profile show projected cost over 3 months?
[03:40] Priya (Redwood): absolutely — we have a "cost simulator" tab. you upload a sample traffic csv and it runs a model matching routine and outputs expected cost for different configs (hosted, dedicated with X GPUs, caching enabled, etc.). i'll attach the spreadsheet after the call.
[03:56] Jordan (Redwood): note we'll also include suggested batching and quantization knobs for latency-sensitive routes; sometimes 8-bit quantization reduces token compute cost without quality loss for certain models.
[04:10] Lena (Suncrest): any risks on quality regression with quant? we care about hallucinations on customer support answers.
[04:18] Priya (Redwood): good point. the console integrates evals — you can run prompt sets and see quality regressions vs baseline. recommend running evals alongside quantized configs in the pilot.
[04:30] Sanjay (Suncrest): security: we need KMS integration and SOC2 docs for procurement. where do those live?
[04:38] Jordan (Redwood): we'll send our security package — SOC2 report, architecture diagram, KMS/HSM integration notes. for Private/VPC deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSMs as part of the Private plan.
[04:52] Mike (Suncrest): any gotchas around VPC peering or network egress? we run everything in GCP and have strict egress controls.
[05:00] Priya (Redwood): the Private deployment model supports VPC peering and on-prem options. for hosted we support VPC connect and IP allowlisting; egress billing varies by region, we can include that in the cost sim. sometimes the transcribe picks up "VPC pearing" — to clarify, it's peering.
[05:18] Jordan (Redwood): we can also run a short smoke benchmark on your peered environment during pilot to validate latency and throughput.
[05:26] Mike (Suncrest): great. on the dashboard you showed latency percentiles, do you expose per-token timing? we want to understand tail latency for long sequences.
[05:36] Priya (Redwood): we do per-token metrics in the trace view. you can see compute vs network time per token, and we break out KV cache hit/miss rates which often explains tail spikes.
[05:48] Lena (Suncrest): can the dashboard show cost per customer end-user or per feature? we sell features to business units and want to chargeback.
[05:56] Priya (Redwood): yes if you instrument requests with tenant/customer IDs, our per-route and per-tag dashboards can roll up cost by tag. most customers create a "feature" tag in headers.
[06:08] Sanjay (Suncrest): how are action audits surfaced — we need audit logs for who changed a rollout or model pin.
[06:15] Jordan (Redwood): Console has an audit trail: user, timestamp, action. it's exportable and integrates with Splunk/Datadog via webhooks. we'll include the retention SLAs in the security pack.
[06:30] Mike (Suncrest): competitor question — we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints, how does Redwood's cost compare?
[06:38] Jordan (Redwood): short answer: depends heavily on traffic profile and sequence length. Redwood focuses on serving optimizations (batching, KV cache, tailored kernels) to reduce per-token compute. in many sustained use cases Dedicated is more economical; we'll model this in the sim.
[06:55] Priya (Redwood): also we can route lower-latency/low-cost requests to smaller models and reserve bigger models for complex queries — routing policies are configurable in the console.
[07:08] Lena (Suncrest): sounds good. can you show the rollout UI quickly?
[07:14] Priya (Redwood): yep — here's the rollout page. you can create canary, percentages by route, automatic rollback on error or degradation thresholds. we show per-metric health charts during rollouts.
[07:30] Mike (Suncrest): this is helpful. what's the typical pilot scope you recommend? 2–4 routes?
[07:38] Priya (Redwood): usually we do 3 routes: one chat, one classification, one rerank or embedding job. that covers seq len variance and different performance profiles. pilot length is 2–4 weeks depending on traffic.
[07:50] Jordan (Redwood): pricing note — pilots are often credit-backed; we'll include pilot pricing in the proposal.
[07:58] Sanjay (Suncrest): for the pilot, we need proof of isolation and KMS integration. is that on the Private side only?
[08:06] Jordan (Redwood): for KMS customer-managed keys we generally require Private, but we can offer limited key wrapping options for Dedicated with strict contracts. we'll detail in the security docs.
[08:18] Mike (Suncrest): ok. last Q from me: can the console alert on drift or quality regressions automatically?
[08:26] Priya (Redwood): yes, quality monitoring can be tied to eval sets and anomaly detection. you can get emailed alerts or webhook triggers when metrics cross thresholds.
[08:36] Lena (Suncrest): perfect. any limitations on export of raw logs for our internal analytics team?
[08:42] Priya (Redwood): you can export raw request logs to your s3/gcs bucket or stream to Kafka. retention policies configurable per plan.
[08:52] Jordan (Redwood): ok folks, wrapping up — recap of next steps: jordan will send pricing and security docs, priya will share benchmark spreadsheet and pilot checklist, mike will provide traffic sample and procurement contact. schedule pilot kickoff for 10/19.
[09:10] Mike (Suncrest): thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[09:14] Jordan (Redwood): thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/console-walkthrough and benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/sheets/benchmarks-xxxx (will replace with live link).

End of Transcript.
